hints: Remember that atomic number always equals the number of protons, and nucleon number equals protons plus neutrons. For an ion, charge equals protons minus electrons.
Recall how to write isotopic symbols as $^{nucleon}_{atomic}\text{X}^{charge}$, using proton number to identify the element from the Periodic Table.
walkthrough:
Decode the lithium ion row**
Look at $^{6}_{3}\text{Li}^{+}$. The bottom number 3 is the atomic number, so you have 3 protons. The top number 6 is the nucleon number, so neutrons = 6 minus 3 = 3. The 1+ charge means 1 electron has been lost, so 3 protons minus 1 = 2 electrons, which matches the table.

Decode the second row from proton number**
You are given 26 protons, so atomic number = 26. That is iron, $\text{Fe}$, from the Periodic Table. Nucleon number = protons + neutrons = $26 + 32 = 58$.

Work out the charge and symbol**
Charge = protons minus electrons = $26 - 23 = +3$. So this is an $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion. Put it together in full isotopic notation: $^{58}_{26}\text{Fe}^{3+}$.

Final answer: Row 1 ($^{6}_{3}\text{Li}^{+}$): nucleon number = 6, number of protons = 3, number of neutrons = 3.
Row 2: atomic number = 26, nucleon number = 58, symbol = $^{58}_{26}\text{Fe}^{3+}$.

hints: Focus on what single particle is being weighed here, one atom of this specific isotope, or one mole of atoms of this isotope.
Remember every relative mass scale in chemistry is fixed against the same standard, an atom of $^{12}\text{C}$ assigned a mass of exactly 12.
walkthrough:
Pin down the sample**
Relative isotopic mass is about one specific isotope, not the natural mixture. Think of picking up a single atom of $^{10}\text{B}$, or one mole of $^{10}\text{B}$ atoms, and weighing it.

Add the relative comparison**
Masses of atoms are far too tiny to use grams directly, so we compare to a standard. By international agreement that standard is carbon-12. We take 1/12 of the mass of one $^{12}\text{C}$ atom as 1 unit, and express the isotope mass relative to that.

Build the precise definition**
Combine both ideas: relative isotopic mass is the mass of an atom of an isotope compared with 1/12 the mass of an atom of carbon-12, which is defined as exactly 12. It has no units because it is a ratio.

Final answer: The mass of an atom of an isotope relative to 1/12 the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
On a scale in which an atom of $^{12}\text{C}$ has a mass of exactly 12 units.

hints: Recall that $A_{r}$ of boron is the weighted average of the two isotopic masses, so $(mass 1 \times \%1 + mass 2 \times \%2)/100 = A_{r}$. Take $A_{r}(\text{B}) = 10.8$ from the Periodic Table.
Let the unknown mass of $^{11}\text{B}$ be $x$ and rearrange the weighted mean equation to solve for $x$.
walkthrough:
Set up the weighted mean**
$A_{r}$ is just the average mass weighted by abundance. For boron with $A_{r} = 10.8$:
$$A_{r} = \frac{\sum (\text{isotopic mass} \times \text{% abundance})}{100}$$
Let the mass of $^{11}\text{B} = x$:
$$\frac{(10.0129 \times 19.78) + (x \times 80.22)}{100} = 10.8$$

Give the answer to the required precision**
The value $10.9941$ already has six significant figures, so no further rounding is needed. Always show your working and check that the answer lies sensibly close to 11, as $^{11}\text{B}$ is the dominant isotope.

Final answer: $$\frac{(10.0129 \times 19.78) + (x \times 80.22)}{100} = 10.8$$
$$x = \frac{1080 - 198.055}{80.22} = 10.9941$$ to six significant figures.
